note_tweet.text:
Obsidian 刚发布面向 AI Agent 的官方 Connectors，支持 Grok Bot、Claude、ChatGPT、Cursor、GitHub Copilot 等主流客户端。

对一人公司来说，最实用的变化是：不用再把笔记反复复制进不同 AI 对话框，多个 Agent 可以基于同一套开源 Skill 规范，共用你本地的 Markdown 知识库。

官方开源仓库（https://t.co/iKV27xhrcr）目前包含 7 个 Skill，按能力分成三层：
1. 格式层：obsidian-markdown、obsidian-bases、json-canvas，教 Agent 正确读写双链、属性、Bases 数据库和白板文件。
2. 操控层：obsidian-cli（直接检索和管理运行中的本地库）、obsidian-headless（无桌面端命令行同步与发布）。
3. 数据管道：defuddle（网页转干净 Markdown）、knap（把 JSON/CSV 按模板渲染成笔记）。

但上生产前必须看清 3 个限制（据官方文档）：
- obsidian-cli 要求电脑本机打开 Obsidian 且开启 CLI，同时 Agent 具备本机命令执行权限；纯云端聊天窗口用不了这一层。
- defuddle、knap、obsidian-headless 并未内置，首次用到时会提示通过 npm 安装。
- 隐私边界：Connector 本身不传数据，但 Agent 读过的笔记都会进入对应模型上下文；敏感资料库务必先单独隔离。

可执行下一步：在 Grok Bot / Cursor 插件目录直接安装 Obsidian，先用测试库跑通一个「网页抓取 → 写入笔记」的最小闭环，再决定是否接入主库。

---

Obsidian just released official Connectors for AI agents—supporting Grok Bot, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and more.

For one-person businesses, the practical shift is clear: instead of copy-pasting notes across tools, multiple agents can now share one local Markdown vault through a single open-source skill pack (https://t.co/iKV27xhrcr).

The pack bundles 7 skills across three layers:
1. File formats: obsidian-markdown, obsidian-bases, and json-canvas (wikilinks, properties, Bases views/formulas, and Canvas files).
2. Vault control: obsidian-cli (search/manage a running desktop vault) and obsidian-headless (CLI sync & publish without the desktop app).
3. Data pipeline: defuddle (clean web-to-Markdown extraction) and knap (render Markdown templates from JSON/CSV).

Three real constraints to note before wiring it into your workflow (per Obsidian's docs):
- obsidian-cli requires the Obsidian desktop app running locally with CLI enabled, plus an agent that can run local commands—cloud-only chat interfaces can't use it directly.
- defuddle, knap, and obsidian-headless aren't bundled; the skill prompts to install them via npm on demand.
- Privacy: connectors don't transmit data on their own, but any note an agent reads enters that model's context. Isolate sensitive vaults first.

Next step: install the Obsidian plugin in Grok Bot or Cursor and test one small loop (web clip → structured note) on a sandbox vault before connecting your main knowledge base.

Docs: obsidian.md/help/connectors

note_tweet.text:
Shiiiit!
My AI agents were supposed to take 90% of my work off my plate. So why am I still the last one in the office? 👀

In reality, Grok Bot saves me 1–2 hours a day. My agents help me in Brand research, finding Gigs, outreach, and put together offers. They also help with editor briefs, early ad concepts, image creation, and transcripts.

I’m still relatively new to marketing. Since moving from art direction into creative strategy/copywriting, I’ve been learning new things every day. And I don’t think that ever stops…

What I like about Grokbot is that I can onboard my agents like real team members. I give each one a name and a role on the team. I share examples, have them watch training videos, and give them feedback on their drafts. I even interview them, and they interview me too. I train them like real employees to run my business! 

Then I decide who gets hired and who gets fired :D

Some of my agents now write copy I can actually use in my ads. But if I blindly trust what they give me, I skip the part where I learn to judge the work for myself. And if I stop developing that judgment, I make myself a lot easier to replace with AI.

AI IS STILL A TOOL. I can onboard my agents like team members, but I’m still the one making the calls.

So I’m automating things bit by bit. I’m happy with every hour my agents save me, and I stay hands-on with the work that helps me grow as a creative strategist.

What have you already automated, and what do you still choose to do yourself?

Let me know in the comments 👇

5 things I think most people get wrong about AI right now:

1/ 80–90% of what you already do may not need automation or an AI agent. At least not within your existing workflows.

2/ Working with AI agents is hard because we still think in tasks, not objectives. Defining the desired outcome is becoming a core professional skill.

3/ One reason we're still struggling with AI ROI after four years is that we expect AI to work like humans. Some processes should be automated. Others should be obliterated and rebuilt from scratch.

4/ Tools like Grok Bot look great in demos and case studies. For many people, they're just another headache until they figure out what to automate and how. Human thinking is still the bottleneck.

5/ Most things companies want to vibe-code could probably be accomplished with an existing skill, plugin, or MCP server.
